core_obligations: Record the local ring square and verify that the fibres of the base change remain locally Noetherian (proof lines 6630-6646).
Prove implication (1) by transferring flatness and Gorensteinness of the fibre along the base change (proof lines 6648-6658).
Prove implications (2) and (3) by using the reverse direction of the Gorenstein base change lemma and, in the third case, the flatness base change lemma for the two flat maps (proof lines 6660-6680).
proof_roadmap: The local ring square and local Noetherianity (proof lines 6630-6646).
difficulty_reason: For f : X -> Y whose fibres are locally Noetherian, a base change Y' -> Y locally of finite type with f' : X' -> Y', and points x' in X' over x in X, the lemma asserts three implications: f Gorenstein at x implies f' Gorenstein at x'; f flat at x together with f' Gorenstein at x' implies f Gorenstein at x; and Y' -> Y flat at f'(x') together with f' Gorenstein at x' implies f Gorenstein at x (statement lines 6613-6628). The proof first notes that the assumption on Y' -> Y makes the residue field extensions finitely generated, so all fibres of f' are locally Noetherian by Varieties, Lemma labelled varieties-lemma-locally-Noetherian-base-change, and records the commutative square of local rings in which the upper left corner is a localisation of the tensor product of the other three (proof lines 6630-6646). For (1), flatness of O_{Y,y} -> O_{X,x} implies flatness of the base changed map by Algebra, Lemma labelled algebra-lemma-base-change-flat-up-down, and Gorensteinness of the fibre O_{X,x}/m_yO_{X,x} passes to the base changed fibre by Lemma labelled lemma-gorenstein-base-change (proof lines 6648-6658). For (2) and (3) the proof uses Lemma labelled lemma-gorenstein-base-change in the opposite direction to deduce that the fibre O_{X,x}/m_yO_{X,x} is Gorenstein, and uses Algebra, Lemma labelled algebra-lemma-base-change-flat-up-down in the third case to transfer flatness from both O_{Y',y'} -> O_{X',x'} and O_{Y,y} -> O_{Y',y'} to O_{Y,y} -> O_{X,x} (proof lines 6660-6680). Reducing each implication to flatness and Gorensteinness of the fibre, and using the two-directional base change lemma for Gorenstein fibres, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
